posts.title: Every fast write moves work somewhere else
posts.description: Every storage engine has to decide what must finish before it tells a client that a write succeeded. The quickest answer is to return after copying the bytes into memory. A local durable write waits for fdatasync() on an SSD in the database host. posts.description: Lately I have been working around sandboxing, storage, and networking, and a lot of that work keeps coming back to files, which makes sense since Unix has organized itself around everything is a file for over fifty years.
